indicator_definition: The unadjusted gender pay gap is the difference between average gross hourly earnings of male and female employees, expressed as a percentage of average gross hourly earnings of male employees. It is based on employees working in firms with ten or more employees. Data are collected through the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES).
rationale: The gender pay gap reflects persistent inequalities between men and women in the labour market, including differences in sectors, occupations, working hours and career interruptions. Closing the gap requires addressing occupational segregation and discrimination. Progress means a sustained reduction in the unadjusted gender pay gap over time.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES), conducted every four years, with annual estimates produced by Eurostat. The indicator covers all economic activities except public administration and is based on gross hourly earnings of employees in establishments with ten or more employees.
